 Fantasy football Week 9 waiver wire: Mike Washington Jr. leads the charge as backfields face major shakeups
 Mike Washington Jr. headlines a busy waiver wire as injuries and shifting backfields create new opportunities for Fantasy managers
 By
 Jamey Eisenberg 
 Nov 3, 2026
 at
 12:03 pm ET 
 •
 10 min read
 Imagn Images Imagn Images 
 As we head into Week 9, three backfields could be changing in Arizona, Las Vegas and the Giants. And if Jonathan Taylor is traded, we could also have a new starter in Indianapolis. It could be a very busy week on the waiver wire. 
 My favorite running back to add this week is Mike Washington Jr. (64 percent rostered on CBS Sports). He took over as the lead running back for the Raiders in Week 8 at the Jets ahead of Ashton Jeanty with a 60-40 split in playing time. If that continues, then Washington is a potential flex option in Week 9 at San Francisco and beyond.
 For the Cardinals, Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Zonovan Knight (concussion) were both injured in Week 8 at Dallas. Tyler Allgeier (45 percent rostered) took over and dominated the Cowboys, and Love was placed on IR on Tuesday. We'll see if Knight can return in Week 9 at Seattle, but Allgeier could be a flex option against the Seahawks. Moving forward, Knight might be the better Arizona running back to add given how he performed so far this season when Love has missed time.
 The Giants had a bye in Week 8, but we saw Cam Skattebo (hamstring) get injured in Week 7, along with Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) placed on injured reserve. Devin Singletary (16 percent rostered) could be the starter in Week 9 at Philadelphia, which would make him a flex option in all leagues.
 We'll also continue to monitor the trade speculation in Indianapolis with Taylor. If he's traded, then Seth McGowan (56 percent rostered) would become a flex option in Week 9 against Dallas. 
This should be a busy week on the waiver wire at running back. But we also have some quarterbacks (Malik Willis and Bo Nix), wide receivers (Antonio Williams and Makai Lemon) and tight ends (Greg Dulcich and Mike Gesicki) who will be impactful as well. 
There are two teams on bye in Week 9, with Pittsburgh and Tennessee and still plenty of injuries to monitor. Get ready to spend some FAAB to make sure those lineups are ready to go.
 Editor's note: For this waiver wire column, we are only looking at players rostered in less than 65 percent of CBS Sports leagues.

 WAIVER WIRE
 Quarterbacks
 On a bye:  Aaron Rodgers and Cam Ward
 Injuries:  Lamar Jackson (thumb), Kyler Murray (hamstring), Tyler Huntley (toe) and Joe Fagnano (knee)
 Check to see if available in shallow leagues:  Sam Darnold (74 percent rostered) and Kirk Cousins (73 percent). Darnold was 17-of-34 passing for 188 yards, two touchdowns and one interception, along with two carries for 20 yards, in Week 8 against the Bears, and this was his best Fantasy outing since Week 2. He now has two favorable upcoming matchups in Week 9 against Arizona and Week 10 against Las Vegas, and Darnold is worth using as a low-end starter in both games. ... Cousins has scored at least 22.5 Fantasy points in six of his past seven games, including three in a row. His upcoming schedule is tough against San Francisco, Seattle, Denver and Cleveland before a bye in Week 13, but Cousins should be considered a low-end starter in those matchups given his level of play this year.
 Drop candidates:  Lamar Jackson (100 percent rostered), Baker Mayfield (55 percent) and Aaron Rodgers (54 percent). Jackson will have surgery on his injured thumb and be placed on IR. It's not yet known if he will miss the rest of the season, but Jackson isn't expected to help Fantasy managers any time soon. Mayfield will likely have to do more than just hand off in Week 9 at Chicago, but that's really all he's done in the past two games against Carolina and Atlanta. He's a combined 7-of-14 passing in his past two outings against the Panthers and Falcons for 64 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions, along with 15 rushing yards. The run game is dominant for Tampa Bay right now, and Mayfield is just a game manager, which isn't good for Fantasy managers. Rodgers has cooled off of late with a combined 19.9 Fantasy points in his past two outings against New Orleans and Cleveland. There's little reason to hold onto him in one-quarterback leagues with the Steelers on bye in Week 9.

Richardson should be added in Superflex and two-quarterback leagues for 1 percent of your remaining FAAB, and he could be a productive Fantasy option if given the starting job.
 WAIVER WIRE
 Running Backs
 On a bye:  Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle, Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears
 Injuries:  Christian McCaffrey (hamstring), Bhayshul Tuten (ankle), Breece Hall (quadriceps), Jeremiyah Love (ankle), Zonovan Knight (concussion), Cam Skattebo (hamstring), Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring), TreVeyon Henderson (illness), RJ Harvey (knee), David Montgomery (groin), Kyle Monangai (thumb), Jadarian Price (chest), Travis Etienne (hamstring), Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), Jeremy McNichols (foot), Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring), Jonathon Brooks (groin), Tyjae Spears (knee), Tank Bigsby (abdomen), Will Shipley (foot), Isiah Pacheco (back) and James Conner (foot)
 Check to see if available in shallow leagues:  Jadarian Price (81 percent rostered), Alvin Kamara (80 percent) and Kaelon Black (68 percent). Price returned in Week 8 against Chicago from his four-game absence with a chest injury and had 10 carries for 29 yards and two catches for 8 yards on four targets. He will share touches with Zach Charbonnet moving forward, but Price can still be a flex option in deeper leagues, especially heading into Week 9 against Arizona. Kamara has scored at least 13.2 PPR points in three of the four games that Etienne was out, and Kamara would be a flex in Week 9 at Cleveland if Etienne can't return. He is eligible to return to practice this week. McCaffrey injured his hamstring in Week 7 at Atlanta before San Francisco's bye in Week 8, and hopefully he's fine for Week 9 against Las Vegas. If McCaffrey is out, then Black would be a must-start running back in all leagues. He has two games this season with double digits in carries, and he scored at least 8.0 PPR points in each outing.
 Drop candidates:  Emanuel Wilson (85 percent rostered), RJ Harvey (78 percent) and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (64 percent). Wilson didn't touch the ball in Week 8 against Chicago with Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price, and it appears like Wilson is the odd man out. You can safely drop him in all leagues. You can stash Harvey on IR, but he's not eligible to return until Week 13 at the earliest. By then, Jonah Coleman could be dominating the Denver backfield. Croskey-Merritt is out for at least two more games, and the earliest he can return is Week 11. Prior to getting hurt, Croskey-Merritt had two games with at least 12.6 PPR points and three games with 7.0 PPR points or less.
